"The massive use of non-nuclear means that cause catastrophes makes a preventive nuclear attack by the Russian Federation possible," Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council , wrote in an article published Monday in the Moscow Journal of International Law and excerpted by the state news agency TASS . Medvedev also warned that "secret or hidden supplies of nuclear weapons from the West to Kyiv will provoke a legitimate preventive nuclear attack by Russia." MOSCOW THREATENS NUCLEAR RESPONSE OVER TINY FORTRESS WEDGED BETWEEN US ALLIES AS CLASH FEARS GROW "Kyiv and its allies must remember that the Russian Federation not only has the right, but in various situations has the obligation to use nuclear weapons," he wrote. Medvedev's warning came amid continuing tensions between Moscow and the West over the nearly five-year war in Ukraine and NATO's military support for Kyiv. He argued that Ukraine and its Western allies have already created circumstances under which Russia could consider a nuclear strike, though he said Russian President Vladimir Putin carefully weighs the consequences before making such a decision. items.summary_original: The House of Representatives' internal watchdog is suggesting a sitting Democrat could have committed criminal sexual assault. An explosive report by the House Ethics Committee released on Monday claimed that Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., violated congressional rules on sexual misconduct by making "unwelcome" advances toward a staffer for the House, disregarding the power imbalance between lawmakers and aides in the process. The report also went a step further, warning Gomez could have violated existing law. Gomez has since announced his intention to resign on Dec. 1. HOUSE DEMOCRAT INVESTIGATED OVER ALLEGED 'INAPPROPRIATE SEXUAL CONTACT' WITH STAFFER The bipartisan panel found that "Representative Gomez knew or had reason to know that his contact was not welcome" when out with the staffer, called "Witness 1," at a D.C. bar. "There is also evidence that he knew or had reason to know his repeated advance towards Witness 1 in his congressional office was inappropriate and unwelcome. Accordingly, Representative Gomez’s conduct towards Witness 1 could implicate D.C. laws related to criminal sexual assault, including misdemeanor sexual abuse," the report said. Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman is leading an 18-state coalition urging the justices to reverse a ruling that blocked the roughly 600-square-foot prayer grotto in Park Hills, Kentucky, despite the project initially receiving approval from local zoning officials. The dispute pits the Missionaries of St. John the Baptist against neighboring property owners Joel and Elizabeth Frederic, who challenged the city's approval of the outdoor shrine and ultimately prevailed in Kentucky's appellate courts. items.summary_original: Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit within less than 60 days according to new Western intelligence assessments reported Monday, raising fears that Moscow is preparing to deploy a weapon capable of crippling thousands of satellites used by the United States and its allies. The intelligence reports emerged just four days after President Donald Trump met with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a high-profile summit in Shenzhen, China, where nuclear arms control was a central topic. The three leaders issued a joint declaration affirming that nuclear war should never be fought, but stopped short of announcing binding arms-control commitments. According to a joint investigation published Nov. 23 by German broadcasters WDR and NDR and the newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung, Western intelligence agencies believe Russia has assembled a satellite known as "Sputnik-S," which has reportedly been stored in the Moscow region for several years. CRUISE COMPANY FOUNDER SAYS HE'S 'THE VILLAIN' AFTER 200-PLUS PASSENGERS ARE STRANDED Almost 15 years ago, on Jan. 13, 2012, the Costa Concordia slammed into rocks off Tuscany’s Giglio island. Schettino reportedly veered off course to perform a "sail-by salute." There were 4,200 passengers and crew on board, and 32 people were killed. Schettino faced backlash after abandoning the ship , while hundreds of passengers were waiting to be rescued. items.summary_original: The politician tasked by Israel's president to form a new government, Gadi Eisenkot, said Monday that Iran poses no immediate threat requiring military action before a new government is formed, drawing a sharp response from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as President Donald Trump considers renewed strikes against Tehran. The dispute comes amid a political power struggle following last month's Israeli election. Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister, but Eisenkot's allies now control the leadership of the Knesset and key parliamentary committees as negotiations over a new government continue. "Today I see no direct and immediate threat to Israel that requires action before a government is formed," Eisenkot, who previously served as the IDF chief of staff, told his party's Knesset faction, according to an English translation of his Hebrew remarks provided to Fox News Digital. ISRAEL'S POLITICAL SHAKE-UP ENTERS NEW PHASE AS FORMER PM PLAYS KINGMAKER — AND DEADLINE LOOMS He stressed that Iran remains Israel's gravest security threat, particularly its nuclear program. "In my view, the gravest threat from Iran is its stockpile of 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%," Eisenkot said. "It has yet to be destroyed or removed." He called for the material at a minimum to be placed under strict monitoring. Netanyahu pushed back hours later, accusing political rivals of downplaying the Iranian threat for political reasons. items.summary_original: Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., triggered online backlash after declining to say "one way or the other" whether the Democratic Party would pursue a government shutdown to advance its agenda during an interview with The New York Times. When asked by The New York Times' Lulu Garcia-Navarro if he would be willing to risk shutting down the government to achieve Democrats' goals, Jeffries declined to rule out the possibility. "I'm not going to say that one way or the other because we got to figure out right now what's possible in terms of the appropriations process," he said. Jeffries said Democrats are now weighing possible restrictions on funding for the Iran war "to make clear that this [war] has to end" ahead of the Dec. 11, 2026, federal funding deadline. HAKEEM JEFFRIES CALLS TRUMP CHIEF OF STAFF STEPHEN MILLER A ‘STONE-COLD RACIST,’ REFUSES TO SIT DOWN WITH HIM "It needs to be over," he said. "In fact, Donald Trump can end it right now. That doesn't mean there's not going to be a lot of work ahead, because Iran is in a stronger position now than they were before this reckless and costly war of choice started." He added the 43-day government shutdown that began in October 2025 was an example of Democrats "not going to go along simply to get along." "That was the longest complete shutdown in American history, and at the end of it, we actually were successful in forcing a vote to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits," he said. S. restrictions, sell oil and petrochemicals, and settle transactions in Russian rubles and Chinese yuan. "Iran’s economy is underwater, and its leaders are panicking," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote in a statement Monday before the news release. "Iran’s shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime. Treasury will continue dismantling these illicit networks until we have buried the head of the snake." items.summary_original: President Donald Trump declared on Monday that he had ordered the military not to detonate degrading lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant unless a court and the Hawkeye State's Democratic Gov.-Elect Rob Sand give the green light for the plan. "I feel the proper course is to get rid of this longterm problem but, at the same time, have ordered the Military not to do so until such time as the Eighth Circuit agrees that we can go forward, and am further making this decision fully subject to the incoming Governor Elect, Rob Sand, agreeing to the operation," Trump declared in part of a lengthy Monday Truth Social post . "If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation," Trump said. The Army had already delayed its plan to detonate the material until Wednesday, once more postponing the explosion expected to send "lead-containing particles" into the air. The detonation was previously scheduled for Friday but was then rescheduled for Monday, with Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle noting in a Thursday statement , "This will delay the detonation until the latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop, which would risk further destabilization of the material." items.summary_original: Connecticut’s effort to impose state rules on federal immigration officers hit a major legal obstacle after a federal judge ruled that the provisions are likely unconstitutional. In a preliminary ruling Friday, U.S. District Judge Vernon D. Oliver blocked Connecticut officials from enforcing certain sections of SB 397 against federal officers while the federal government’s lawsuit over the law continues. The blocked provisions of the law, passed in May, set statewide use-of-force standards, gave state officials authority to investigate and prosecute certain cases involving federal officers — such as excessive use-of-force incidents — and restricted federal officers’ use of face coverings. Oliver wrote that the sections likely violate the Constitution’s supremacy clause, which limits states’ ability to control federal operations. DHS, DEM OFFICIALS CLASH AFTER ICE ARREST AT SEATTLE AIRPORT The case underscores a broader legal fight over how far states and cities can go in regulating federal officers who operate within their borders. Federal judges have already blocked state and local restrictions on federal officers in Virginia , New York and Philadelphia. Most recently, a federal judge in California entered a permanent injunction barring enforcement of challenged state mask and identification laws against federal officers. items.summary_original: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to address President Donald Trump’s efforts to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive officer at NVIDIA, exiting a press conference without taking any questions on Monday. "Is Jensen Huang’s reinstatement a national security risk?" Rubio was asked by reporters as he met with the Qatari prime minister at the State Department. He turned around and walked away without answering. His abrupt departure comes on the heels of statements from Trump, confirming that the president and the vice president had helped persuade NVIDIA to reinstate Huang — despite lingering concerns among some of the administration's cabinet members about the company’s efforts to safeguard sensitive intelligence. A source familiar told Fox News that President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance worked over the weekend to reinstate Huang after they received security briefings and became convinced that Huang did not present a national security threat in his role as CEO. In recent days, Vance worked with figures in Silicon Valley and higher-ups at Nvidia to urge the board to reinstate him, the source said. The source also said the administration viewed Huang's support for open-source AI as a backstop against major AI companies accruing uncontested capabilities behind closed doors — a rare position among AI executives. items.summary_original: Former Mossad chief David Barnea revealed Monday that Israeli intelligence played a key role in thwarting an ISIS-inspired terrorist plot targeting Taylor Swift's concerts in Vienna in 2024, an attack he said could have killed hundreds of young people. Speaking at the European Leadership Network ELNET conference in Jerusalem , Barnea disclosed that Austrian intelligence had initially identified the threat before turning to Israel's Mossad, which helped uncover the network behind the planned attack. "The initial threat warning came from our Austrian partners," Barnea said, according to the transcript of his speech. SPY LAW USED TO STOP TAYLOR SWIFT ATTACK TO LAPSE AS CONGRESS SKIPS TOWN, WORLD CUP NEARS Once Austrian authorities shared the information, the Mossad used its intelligence capabilities to analyze the threat, uncover the network and help bring about the suspects' arrests, Barnea said. The joint effort prevented "mass murder, up to hundreds of young European men and women," he said. The disclosure sheds new light on the international intelligence cooperation behind the foiled plot , which forced the cancellation of three sold-out shows during Swift's record-breaking "Eras Tour" in August 2024. More than 170,000 spectators were expected to attend the concerts, according to estimates from the Austrian news agency APA cited by The Times of Israel. "در حالی که DNC صلاحیت قانونی برای ممنوعیت سوپر PAC ها یا گروه های پول تاریک را ندارد، ما از نامزدهای خود می خواهیم که دخالت خود در انتخابات ریاست جمهوری دموکرات را محکوم کنند.
items.summary_original: The 2028 election season is already off to the races. The Democratic Party released its rules of engagement for the next presidential primary season on Monday morning, outlining a framework for 12 debates and setting barriers for candidates hoping to compete. One key rule will have Democratic presidential hopefuls swear off dark money during the course of the primary election. "In the wake of the Citizens United Supreme Court decision, dark money and independent spending have exploded, increasing the influence of special interests in politics ," a press release by the Democratic National Committee (DNC) said. "While the DNC does not have the legal authority to ban super PACs or dark money groups, we are requiring our candidates to denounce their involvement in the Democratic presidential primary, in line with Democratic Party values and our 2024 Platform, in order to qualify for the debate stage." HOUSE COMMITTEE PASSES FOREIGN FUNDING TRANSPARENCY ACT TO EXPOSE FOREIGN DONATIONS TO NONPROFITS That includes money earned by both super PACs and 501(c)(4) nonprofit organizations during the course of the entire primary. And the rule, according to a framework obtained by Fox News Digital, will rely largely on Democrats' own self-reporting. Each campaign must designate a go-between with the DNC whose job is to specifically identify and report spending by outside dark money groups . items.summary_original: FIRST ON FOX: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) awarded millions of taxpayer dollars to foreign animal research facilities where significant biosafety, containment and staffing failures allegedly took place — including a bat virus experiment in Australia that was abruptly halted after animal containment broke down, according to federal records obtained by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) and reviewed by Fox News Digital. The internal agency records and noncompliance reports show that federal health officials repeatedly approved funding or failed to identify major safety and oversight vulnerabilities until after taxpayer-funded animal experiments were already underway. items.summary_original: The war between Russia and Ukraine continues to spill outside the countries' boundaries, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy shared a video of a drone striking and sinking Russian weapons ships off the coast of Libya. "We continue our operations in designated waters," Zelenskyy wrote early Monday morning in a statement on X. "We are responding to Russia’s aggression. We are developing Ukraine weapons. Glory to Ukraine!" The strikes come as President Donald Trump is pushing for peace, but Ukraine has remained steadfast in not only fighting off Russian gains in south and east of Ukraine, but also taking the fight to Russia "in designated waters" around the globe. RUSSIAN WARSHIP SINKS OFF LIBYA AS SUSPECTED UKRAINIAN STRIKES TAKE WAR BEYOND BLACK SEA "An exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war," the post began. "I thank the warriors of the Security Service of Ukraine and all our Defense Forces of Ukraine who took part in carrying out these tasks. I received detailed briefings on the operation’s steps yesterday and today – the targets we set were achieved. It all took place off the coast of Libya. "Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones . Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk. It’s one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war. A Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed along with the corvette. Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGAR

items.summary_original: EXCLUSIVE : Oregon's lone Republican congressman told Fox News Digital that voters in his district rejected what he described as the state's "failed" progressive policies, offering the GOP a roadmap for winning back voters after Democrats' midterm sweep. Rep. Cliff Bentz, R-Ore., who won his fourth term in Congress by over 70,000 votes, with a total of 61% of the vote, made his remarks after securing re-election despite a nationwide Democratic wave that handed Republicans significant losses in Congress and state elections. "My folks wanted someone that they could depend upon when it comes to protecting business and trying to reverse this horrible trend toward more, in this you have a failed state than anything else," Bentz told Fox News Digital. FLORIDA CONGRESSMAN DIAGNOSES GOP'S BLUE TSUNAMI LOSSES: 'WE FAILED TO MAKE THEM THINK WE CARED ABOUT THEM' The congressman argued that his continued electoral success stems from highlighting what he considers the economic consequences of Democratic leadership in Oregon , particularly policies enacted in the state capital. "Crazy, crazy Democrat policies emanating out of Salem, the capital of Oregon," Bentz said, pointing to what he described as "the ridiculous impact of these policies." Bentz blamed high taxes and progressive regulations for hurting businesses and contributing to Oregon's declining quality of life, arguing that voters are increasingly frustrated with the state's political direction. items.summary_original: Sen. John Kennedy , R-La., is continuing to leave the door open to the possibility of mounting a 2028 presidential bid, though he said that such a move is "not likely" and that he plans to seek re-election. "My plan right now is to run for re-election," Kennedy told Kristen Welker during an interview that aired on NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday. "If I get fed up with things and catch a wild hair and have a, I don't know, a spontaneous moment of ... questionable genius, if I get really fed up I could run. But it's not likely," he said, noting that he plans to pursue re-election. DEMOCRATS SIZE UP 2028 IN DENVER. WE ASKED WHO'S READY TO RUN Kennedy has served in the Senate since early 2017. His current term ends in early 2029, so if he wants to seek a third Senate term, he will need to run in 2028. President Donald Trump , who is currently serving his second term, is constitutionally barred from being elected president again. REPUBLICAN SENATOR OPENS DOOR ON POSSIBILITY OF A PRESIDENTIAL BID, IN SHIFT FROM PAST POSITION During a "Meet the Press" interview that aired last month, Kennedy also told Welker that he planned to seek re-election. "But as I've said before," he told Welker last month regarding the idea of a presidential run, "if I don't think I can be effective in the Senate anymore I would consider it." items.summary: اولین شبکه فاکس — رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ با گاوین نیوسام فرماندار کالیفرنیا به خاطر طرح گسترده اش برای معافیت 548 محکوم به اعدام از اعدام، از جمله مردی که 9 نفر از اعضای خانواده خود را به قتل رساند، قاتل پولی کلاس 12 ساله و مردی که به دلیل شکنجه گابرییل 8 ساله محکوم شد، مقابله خواهد کرد. کاخ سفید به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال تایید کرد که انتظار می‌رود ترامپ بعدازظهر دوشنبه در کنار تاد بلانچ، دادستان کل و کش پاتل، مدیر اف‌بی‌آی در وزارت دادگستری (DOJ) حضور یابد تا تخفیف‌های پیشنهادی فرماندار دموکرات را محکوم کند. انتظار می‌رود خانواده‌های قربانیان قتل در این مراسم شرکت کنند، جایی که داستان‌های آنها برجسته می‌شود، زیرا دولت ترامپ تلاش‌های نیوسام را برای جایگزینی هر حکم اعدام کالیفرنیا با حبس ابد به چالش می‌کشد.
items.summary_original: FIRST ON FOX — President Donald Trump will confront California Gov. Gavin Newsom over his sweeping plan to spare 548 death row inmates from execution, including a man who murdered nine members of his own family, the killer of 12-year-old Polly Klaas and the man convicted of torturing 8-year-old Gabriel Fernandez to death. Trump is expected to appear alongside Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel at the Department of Justice (DOJ) on Monday afternoon to condemn the Democratic governor's proposed commutations, the White House confirmed to Fox News Digital. Families of murder victims are expected to attend the event, where their stories will be highlighted as the Trump administration challenges Newsom's effort to replace every California death sentence with life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. NEWSOM'S BID TO EMPTY CALIFORNIA'S DEATH ROW COLLIDES WITH VOTERS' REPEATED REJECTION OF ABOLITION "Governor Newsom is failing the victims and their families by refusing to carry out justice against these barbaric child killers and serial killers. These murderers raped, tortured and terrorized innocent victims. Governor Newsom must stop playing politics with public safety," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. Newsom announced Nov. 5 that he intended to commute all 548 California death sentences to life imprisonment without parole, arguing that capital punishment is incompatible with the state's values. items.summary_original: Talk about talking turkey. Two feathered VIPs have checked into one of Washington's most luxurious hotels, complete with plush beds, a red-carpet welcome and a crowd of eager photographers, ahead of President Donald Trump's annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon at the White House. The presidential hopefuls arrived Sunday at the historic Willard InterContinental Washington, D.C., where they were photographed strutting across a red carpet, posing for pictures and standing atop the hotel's beds before their big day on the South Lawn. THE PENNSYLVANIA FARM BEHIND A WHITE HOUSE THANKSGIVING TURKEY TRADITION The U.S. Department of Agriculture celebrated their arrival on X, announcing a "SPECIAL DELIVERY TO WASHINGTON, D.C.!" and describing the birds as "two VERY special guests" receiving the presidential treatment. Photographs shared by the USDA, credited to the White House and National Turkey Federation, showed the plump white birds making their grand entrance before an audience of hotel guests and photographers. One turkey was even pictured riding through the hotel's ornate hallways inside a travel crate perched on a brass luggage cart. The pair appeared equally comfortable with the accommodations, with one bird spreading its feathers atop a neatly made bed while its companion stood nearby. items.summary_original: A Democratic New York City assemblyman addressed bizarre "lizard people" conspiracy theories after a viral video appeared to show his eyes rolling backward while standing behind Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a press conference. Jordan J.G. Wright was spotted during a press conference behind Mamdani on Friday, when the city announced plans to eventually shut down Rikers Island. As Mamdani spoke, Wright appeared to flash a slight grin before blinking and rolling his eyes in a circular motion toward the back of his head, prompting a wave of bizarre speculation online. "I have no idea what was going on in that video. I’m really not sure," Wright told the New York Post in a statement. NYC MAYOR MAMDANI ANNOUNCES DELAYED PLAN TO CLOSE CITY'S LARGEST JAIL He added that his work as an assemblyman speaks to his human character, pointing to a project he championed in Harlem that serves as the city's first community-based center dedicated to climate action. The five-story hub provides residents with environmental education and advocacy. "Obviously I’m a human being, and my humanity can be seen through my legislation like the $4 million for the WE ACT environmental justice center in Harlem," he said. "I can’t speak to any reptiles or aliens." The video sent social media users into a frenzy over the weekend, reigniting a decades-old conspiracy theory that extraterrestrial reptilians secretly control the Earth by disguising themselves as world leaders and celebrities to manipulate society. items.summary_original: A Russian warship capsized and sank Sunday after suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck a naval base in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire, according to Libyan officials. Hours later, a second drone attack also hit a commercial ship off the coast of Benghazi, Reuters reported. The first ship, the Russian navy corvette Merkury, was docked at Benghazi Naval Base when two explosive-laden sea drones struck the vessel, according to Libyan military officials who spoke to The Associated Press . UKRAINE POUNDS BLACK SEA FLEET’S ‘LAST MAJOR STRONGHOLD’ WHILE PUTIN FLEXES NAVAL POWER IN PACIFIC At least four other drones were intercepted and destroyed, the officials said. Satellite images showed most of the warship capsized and submerged, with only its bow remaining above water. Smoke could be seen rising from the ship's superstructure, and debris was scattered along the pier. Ten people, including Russian and Libyan nationals, suffered minor injuries in the attack and were receiving treatment in Benghazi, medical sources told Reuters. The warship had stopped at the port to refuel and resupply while returning to Russia under a maritime cooperation agreement with Libya's eastern-based government, officials said in a statement. Libyan military officials said an initial investigation indicated that Ukrainian sea drones had been launched from a base in western Libya , according to The AP. UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA’S ARCTIC GAS HEARTLAND AS TRUMP PUSHES PUTIN TOWARD PEACE

The reported operation would involve tankers sailing from Kharg Island, which handles most of Iran's crude oil exports, toward the Gulf of Oman and with crews reportedly assigned to the vessels and Iranian flags raised ahead of a possible attempt to breach the blockade. items.summary_original: Armenia is set to launch a U.S.-backed transportation and energy project along Iran's northern border Monday, despite warnings from a senior Iranian official that Tehran would "break their legs" if President Donald Trump and his allies crossed the Islamic Republic's "red line." Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan confirmed that the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project would launch Monday, advancing the plan to connect mainland Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave through southern Armenia and establish energy links with Turkey and Azerbaijan, Turkish media reported, citing Interfax. The project, a centerpiece of a U.S.-brokered peace initiative between Armenia and Azerbaijan, would also expand American economic involvement in the South Caucasus, where Iran has warned against any development it believes could threaten its security or regional influence. TRUMP'S FIRST IRAN WAR ESCALATION POST-MIDTERM LOSSES SEEKS TO CHOKE OFF TEHRAN’S TRADE The corridor has also gained strategic significance amid the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, as Tehran seeks to secure its northern trade routes and limit the U.S. security presence near its borders while Washington maintains its naval blockade and Task Force Iron Gate focuses on Iran's borders. Speaking at the DigiTec 2026 technology conference in Yerevan, Pashinyan said the new TRIPP initiative, also known as the "Trump Corridor," would strengthen Armenia's regional energy connections, according to Interfax .

items.summary_original: Democrats have stormed back into power in the House, securing the largest majority of any party since 1992 in a sweeping midterm victory that will reshape the balance of power in Washington and leave Republicans with significantly less influence over the chamber. The victory was cemented after Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the House from North Carolina, according to The Associated Press (AP). He defeated longtime Republican incumbent Rep. Virginia Foxx, who chaired the powerful House Rules Committee, which determines which bills reach the House floor for a vote. With several general election results still being called, Democrats have picked up 44 seats so far, giving them at least 258 seats in the House, their largest majority in more than three decades, according to The AP. STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE Meanwhile, Republicans have been left with at least 173 seats. Four House races remain undecided in Minnesota, Tennessee and two December runoffs in Louisiana, according to The AP. The party's projected majority will surpass its post-election totals in every election since Bill Clinton first won the presidency in 1992, when Democrats secured 258 seats, the outlet said. The party's next-largest showing reportedly came in 2008, when Barack Obama was elected president and Democrats won 257 House seats. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump is warning that he is inclined to order military strikes against Iran after the new year if the two countries fail to reach an agreement, dismissing ongoing diplomatic talks with Tehran as meaningless. In exclusive comments Sunday to Fox News, the president accused Iranian negotiators of stalling while continuing to escalate hostilities following the U.S. elections. TRUMP KEEPS SIGNALING AN END TO IRAN WAR, BUT EXPERT WARNS A CRUCIAL PIECE OF HIS STRATEGY IS MISSING "They’re more aggressive now than before the election," Trump said, characterizing Iranian officials as "professional tap dancers." "They talk all the time, all they do is talk, but it’s all b------," he added. The remarks come as the U.S. maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports amid broader conflict in the Strait of Hormuz , and as Trump predicted that tit-for-tat strikes will continue between American and Iranian forces. PROTESTERS CALL FOR REGIME CHANGE IN IRAN FOLLOWING DEADLY CRASH THAT KILLED 13 OIL AND GAS WORKERS Trump also dared Tehran to challenge the U.S. naval siege. "I hope they do, they’ll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy," Trump said regarding the possibility of Iranian forces testing the blockade. Meanwhile, anti-government demonstrations have flared up again in several Iranian cities. Asked about the renewed unrest inside the country, Trump offered a direct message to demonstrators on the ground: "Keep protesting."

items.summary_original: House Democrats are pushing to raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour, calling the current hourly pay a "remnant of slavery" to "oppress women," despite warnings from conservative economists that the proposal could drive up costs and threaten jobs. The proposal from the Congressional Progressive Caucus would more than triple the current $7.25 federal minimum wage, raising questions about its potential impact on businesses and workers in states with significantly lower living costs than major cities. "We should be rallying around (a minimum wage of) $25 at minimum, and it should be cost adjusted for inflation , so that people can have a job that enables them to survive and thrive," Rep. Everton Blair Jr., D-Ga., told Fox News Digital. AOC-BACKED $25 MINIMUM WAGE PLAN SOUNDS GREAT — BUT AT WHAT COST? Asked whether a nationwide $25 minimum wage could hurt workers and businesses in lower-cost states, Blair argued that the proposed rate should serve as a national baseline. The congressman said $25 an hour should be "the floor" and "should be higher in places with a higher cost of living." Blair acknowledged concerns that raising the minimum wage could contribute to inflation but said lawmakers must find a way to increase workers' earnings while "keeping people afloat." Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., echoed Blair's support for the proposal, pointing to the high cost of living in cities such as Seattle and Washington, D.C., as justification for raising wages. Bolsonaro said that he fled for the sake of Brazil, to continue the fight against Alexandre de Moraes and the Brazilian Supreme Court, and alleging both election interference and political persecution. During the arrest, other travelers began getting in the officers' way, and one passenger threw hot coffee at the agents, DHS said. items.summary_original: A massive fire tore through a three-story candy factory in Indonesia's Banten province, killing at least three workers and likely more, and leaving dozens of others unaccounted for as emergency crews fought persistent hotspots into Sunday. Indonesian police removed 24 body bags amid battling the smoldering fire and pausing a search for missing workers overnight, which will resume Monday morning. There were reportedly as many as 300 present for their Saturday shift, but the factory said 24 of the 65 workers involved had returned home, four were receiving medical treatment, 29 remained missing and the whereabouts of another eight had yet to be confirmed. Body bags might contain remains from several people because the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable, police said. The fire broke out at 5 p.m. local time Saturday at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia facility in the Cikande area of the Serang district, which borders the capital, Jakarta. CHINA FIREWORKS FACTORY EXPLOSION: VIDEO CAPTURES DEVASTATING AFTERMATH OF BLAST THAT LEFT AT LEAST 26 DEAD "We have concluded that the victims of this fire cannot be identified through visual inspection," Wahyu Hidayati, a police disaster victim identification official, said. Authorities are collecting DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers. The identification process could take two to three weeks, Hidayati added. items.summary_original: A lawsuit challenging Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom's plan to commute 548 death sentences is raising questions about the governor's clemency powers, with a legal expert arguing Newsom is using his gubernatorial authority to circumvent the will of voters who have repeatedly rejected efforts to abolish capital punishment. Newsom announced Nov. 5 that he intends to commute the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the Golden State's death row to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole, a move that will take effect only after the necessary legal steps are completed. The Criminal Justice Legal Foundation (CJLF) on Sunday filed a lawsuit at the California Supreme Court seeking to block Newsom's proposed sweeping commutation, citing the governor's "failure to provide legally required notice to district attorneys and his disregard for the rights of victims and their families to be notified and heard," according to a news release. Newsom may be using clemency to impose his own views on capital punishment despite voters repeatedly rejecting abolition, Zack Smith, a senior legal fellow for Courts and the Constitution at the Heritage Foundation, told Fox News Digital on Tuesday. The investors allege that Spanish construction giant ACS and companies to tied its former subsidiary Cobra, misled federal officials into approving the grant by claiming the troubled solar plant was ready for use, even though it had suffered major construction problems and was shut down for months following a molten-salt-tank failure. items.summary_original: A Jewish American activist in New York City decried what he calls "anti-Jewish discrimination" after the student government at a school that is part of the City University of New York (CUNY) system, canceled an event that was supposed to include the school's Hillel group when it received backlash from other student organizations. Hunter College's undergraduate student government (USG) canceled a "Cultural Arts Night" involving several student groups, including Hunter Hillel, the Chinese Student Scholar Association, the Taiwanese Student Association and the Center for Puerto Rican Studies, according to the New York Post . The radical far-left group Students for Justice in Palestine reportedly took part in planning the event. In a statement to The Post, the school itself admitted that some of those groups withdrew from the event because Hunter Hillel was planning to participate. items.summary_original: Red hammer-and-sickle flags flew over Europe at protests across the continent Friday, but media coverage barely mentioned them. Media outlets described the day's demonstrations as "youth protests" over wages, schools, climate, "austerity" and the alleged "genocide" in Israel. The streets told a different story. A Fox News Digital investigation reveals that a transnational network of self-described communist, Marxist and socialist groups organized the protests with an explicitly ideological appeal of using party banners, mass-produced recruitment posters and calls for a "communist mass movement" and "socialist revolution." CHAOS INC.: WHO'S WHO IN THE GLOBAL MAYHEM NETWORK? COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE Officials in Hamburg, Germany, warned that "left-wing extremist" groups were behind Friday's actions. In Milan, a young woman wore a red hammer-and-sickle shirt, raising her fist among demonstrators holding placards that read "FIGHT FOR OUR FUTURE" above small branding for Youth International Strike Against War, the socialist coalition that organized the day's actions. By late Friday, the protests were promoted by BreakThrough News, a nonprofit funded by Neville Roy Singham, an American-born communist tech tycoon living in Shanghai, supporting the Chinese Communist Party and President Xi Jinping's "new world order." items.summary_original: One of the FBI's Ten Most Wanted fugitives has been captured in Mexico after a joint U.S.-Mexico operation during which the arresting force "came under attack with gunfire and explosives," authorities announced Saturday. Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, described by the FBI as the "alleged leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization, a heavily armed, major drug-trafficking organization based in Sinaloa, Mexico," was detained in the city of Guasave. The State Department previously issued a $5 million reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of Meza-Flores, who went by the alias "Chapo Isidro." ALLEGED JALISCO CARTEL LEADER ACCUSED OF DRUG TRAFFICKING AND FUEL SMUGGLING ARRESTED IN MEXICO Mexico's Secretariat of National Defense said Meza-Flores was detained during a military raid carried out by special forces personnel. U.S. and Mexican intelligence agencies coordinated in the lead-up to the operation, which also netted the arrests of the cartel's second in command and a financial operator. "The operation to carry out these arrests was conducted by elite military forces, which, after precisely locating the target using various technological tools, carried it out in three phases, as follows," the Secretariat of National Defense wrote on X. items.summary_original: Ukraine 's repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge, one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's most prized infrastructure projects, have dealt a potentially significant blow to Moscow's military supply routes into occupied Crimea, raising questions about Russia's ability to sustain operations as both sides prepare for a difficult winter. A European intelligence assessment dated Nov. 18 and obtained by Fox News Digital describes Ukraine's latest assault as likely its most successful attack on the heavily defended crossing, following a coordinated campaign targeting Russian air defenses, radar and electronic warfare systems. Ret. Gen. Philip Breedlove, former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe, told Fox News Digital the consequences could extend far beyond the destruction of a symbolic Russian landmark. "The Russians are extremely limited in how they get supplies to Crimea and cutting the Kerch bridge will severely, severely damage their ability to resupply Crimea," Breedlove said. The massive overnight assault Friday came as the Trump administration announced progress toward expanding peace negotiations with Russia, exposing the stark contrast between the diplomatic optimism emerging from Thursday's meetings and the escalating war on the ground. A European intelligence source told Fox News Digital that Putin is preparing an intensified winter military campaign and believes that a combination of sustained battlefield pressure and U.S.-led diplomatic negotiations could eventually force Ukraine to surrender additional territory. According to the source, Russia's calculation is that Ukraine could be compelled to accept territorial concessions by spring, particularly in the country's east. items.summary_original: The Republican chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee has warned of an ongoing ‘horrific trend’ of Christians being killed in Africa . Earlier this month, at least 34 people, the majority said to be Ethiopian Orthodox Christians, were killed in a village in the Arsi Zone, about 250 miles southeast of Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa. "The attacks on Christians in Ethiopia are a horrific trend," Sen. Jim Risch, R-Idaho, told Fox News Digital in a statement, adding, "The instability and violence in Ethiopia has grave consequences for Ethiopian civilians, the region and American interests." NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES Open Doors UK Ireland told Fox News Digital there has been a string of killings in the area, with some 60 Orthodox Christians killed just two weeks before this attack in November. Open Doors is an international organization supporting persecuted Christians. A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital they are aware of "reports of killing in Arsi Zone," adding: "Reports of civilian killings in Ethiopia demand action. We call for independent investigations and accountability." The Addis Standard online news outlet reported gunmen approached St. Mary’s Church in Endeto, Robe District, and at the main entrance shouted "Surrender" before opening fire. items.summary_original: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling on the U.S. to quickly organize talks with Russia with the full participation of European negotiators and advisors in what would mark a first-of-its-kind meeting. He made the call Thursday after meeting with several U.S. and European leaders in Berlin at the Coalition of the Willing summit, which focused on security guarantees aimed at deterring future Russian aggression. During the meeting, U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner announced that Moscow and President Donald Trump had agreed to a multilateral negotiating format involving Europe. "We are counting on the American side to help organize the first multilateral meeting at the team level, with full European participation, as soon as possible," Zelenskyy said. The push signals an effort to prevent Europe and Kyiv from being sidelined in U.S.-Russia talks . KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE "From the very beginning, Ukraine has advocated for this approach — maximum coordination among us on everything concerning European and Ukrainian security and our future," Zelenskyy said. "We need to work quickly, and this is the only approach Ukraine is taking. The more actively the discussions move forward, the greater the chances of achieving real progress." items.summary_original: Two Iranian twin sisters imprisoned for participating in anti-government protests came face-to-face with the very official they accused of torturing and sexually assaulting them when they appeared in court to seek justice. They discovered he was the judge assigned to hear their complaint, their U.S.-based cousin told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview. Masoud Nourmohammadi, the cousin of Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, alleged that the official had been involved in their interrogation and subsequently presided over the complaint they filed against the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). "As soon as they walk in, they see the exact person who tortured them and sexually assaulted them is the judge," Nourmohammadi said. IRAN'S REGIME CAME FOR TEENAGE TWINS; THEIR FATE OFFERS A GLIMPSE OF TEHRAN'S WIDENING DEATH CAMPAIGN He claimed the complaint was immediately dismissed by that same official. "The judge was their prosecutor during the building (of) the case, and he was the one that did the sexual assault on the kids and tortured them as a prosecutor and for the lawsuit he was assigned as a judge for that lawsuit," Nourmohammadi said. Fox News Digital has not independently verified the allegations or reviewed the court documents. The twins, now 21, were arrested after January anti-government demonstrations in Isfahan . items.summary_original: A "terrorist attack" by the Iran-backed Houthis damaged multiple floors at the tallest skyscraper in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which houses the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund on Thursday, authorities and reports said. Entrances leading into the King Abdullah Financial District were closed and people were being evacuated from the area following the strike by a suspected Houthi missile, according to Reuters. The news agency reported that the attack on the Public Investment Fund Tower, which is 80 stories tall, destroyed windows across up to eight floors of the building and bent portions of its metal facade.
